findings.title: Login-cache invalidation uses the org-aware isEnabled wrapper
findings.body: update() loads the previous provider with getById() and passes that object into registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate. With the organization feature on, getById() does not return the stored model: it returns an anonymous IdentityProviderModel whose isEnabled() is false when the IdP is linked to an organization that is missing, disabled, or whose OrganizationProvider is disabled, even if the IdP's own enabled flag is still true. LoginFilter.ENABLED is IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled, so getLoginPredicate() fails for that wrapper. The method then returns without registering any .idp.login.* invalidation when both sides fail the predicate. That is exactly the in-session path (getByAlias/getById, mutate, update) while the org is disabled, and it also happens for an admin update whose raw model no longer qualifies (hide-on-login, link-only, enabled=false, kc.org.broker.public cleared, or organizationId moved) if the wrapped original already fails the predicate. The cached id set keeps the old membership until expiry. After the organization is enabled again, getForLogin still serves that set, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hide-on-login, link-only, or broker-public. IdPs that were configured to stay off the login page, including non-public organization brokers, can be offered for login. Compare the delegate/raw model (and null-check it) instead of the organization-aware wrapper.

findings.title: Login-cache test cleans up the wrong IdP alias
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin creates providers with aliases idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-20, but every cleanup is registered as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (the loop at line 381 and idp-alias-20 at line 425). The admin-client get() receiver is bound immediately, so cleanup DELETEs the nonexistent alias "alias" and never removes the providers this test created. Those IdPs remain in the shared realm. The test asserts exact cache sizes (5, 6, 10, 11), so a rerun, or testCacheIDPByOrg running first (it has the same get("alias") cleanup and leaves public org-idp-* brokers linked to orga), changes those counts and can fail this test or later organization tests.
